subject: [Urgent] Elevated 5xx/429 spike after model v2.1 rollout - exec brief requested
messages:
From: Lena Cho <lena@glaciertech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Prod: sudden 5xx/429 spike after model update

Hi Jonas / Monica,

We're seeing a sharp spike in 5xx and 429s starting ~07:50 UTC after you rolled model v2.1 into serving for our account. Throughput dropped; many of our clients are hitting timeouts and piling up retries. Key observations from our side: 
- 5xx rate increased from ~0.4% to 6.8% over 15 minutes.
- 429s rose in lockstep with CPU/GPU utilization bursts on a subset of hosts.
- Error samples show "kernel_dispatch_failed" and "kv-cache-miss" traces.

I've attached a short sample log and a KV cache trace. Can you confirm whether this rollout included the new quantization profile or kernel selector change? This is impacting our customer SLAs; we need an immediate rollback if safe.

Please escalate to engineering and leadership — this needs exec visibility.

Thanks,
Lena Cho
SRE Lead, Glacier Tech

Attachments: glacier-5xx-429-sample.log, kvcache-trace-20260415.json

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lena Cho <lena@glaciertech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-15T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Prod: sudden 5xx/429 spike after model update

Lena — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. I'm escalating and coordinating now. TL;DR: we saw the same spike in our telemetry; we're initiating an immediate rollback to model v2.0 on Glacier's routing pool unless you object.

What I see so far from infra: 
- v2.1 rollout included a new quantization profile (q4_1) and a small kernel selector tweak intended to improve latency for long sequences.
- The rollout target was a narrow pool of instances serving Glacier (canary-style).
- After the change, a subset of requests triggered repeated KV cache misses, causing repeated decoder work and higher GPU kernel throughput. That combined with client retry behavior created a retry storm and transient OOM/kernel_dispatch failures on a few hosts, which is producing amplified 5xx/429 signals.

Immediate actions we're proposing (can start within minutes):
1) Roll back to model v2.0 (previous quant profile + kernels) on Glacier's routing pool — expected to restore baseline.
2) Apply short-term rate-limits and stronger client-side backoff guidance to Glacier to reduce retry amplification while rollback completes.
3) Collect full traces from the affected hosts for a post-mortem; avoid destructive debug on prod.

Marissa/Evelyn/Markus — please confirm and advise if you want a different mitigation. Aditya — flagging for exec awareness; we may need to offer credits if this breaches Glacier's SLA.

I'll post status updates here and attach the rollback steps once started.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-04-15T09:30:00Z
Subject: Rollback started — initial observations and mitigation steps

Team / Lena — rollback to v2.0 began at 09:18 UTC on Glacier's routing pool. Initial notes: 
- Rollback initiated via orchestration controller; we reverted quantization profile and kernel selector flags for the affected pool.
- Within ~6 minutes the request success rate started improving on the primary hosts; 5xx/429 rates are trending down but not yet back to baseline.
- We observed heavy connection churn and a continued stream of retries from client-side SDKs; we're asking Glacier to temporarily increase client backoff jitter and cap retry attempts to 3.

Attached: rollback-notes.txt with exact steps performed and the list of hosts patched. We're also collecting kernel-level device traces and a distilled KV cache hit/miss histogram for the last hour.

Next: Evelyn and infra will review traces for any deeper regression introduced by the q4_1 profile and the kernel selector. If rollback does not fully stabilize within 30–45 minutes we'll consider draining the affected hosts and re-provisioning.

— Jonas

Date: 2026-04-15T11:05:00Z
Subject: Exec escalation summary for Aditya / leadership

Aditya — quick summary for execs and recommended next steps to contain customer impact and limit financial exposure.

What happened (summary):
- A canary rollout of model v2.1 (quant profile q4_1 + kernel selector change) on Glacier's pool triggered repeated KV cache misses for certain request patterns. That led to higher per-request token processing, increased GPU kernel contention, and transient kernel_dispatch failures on a subset of hosts. Client retry behavior amplified the load, causing a visible spike in 5xx/429 errors and reduced throughput from 07:50–09:30 UTC.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rollback to model v2.0 completed (09:18 start; 09:28 bulk completion for the pool).
- Temporary client-side retry guidance provided to Glacier and request caps suggested.
- Collected device/kernel traces and KV cache histograms for post-mortem.
